questions.question:
The intensity of the light from a bulb incident on a surface is $0.22W{m}^{ - 2}$. The amplitude of the magnetic field in this light-wave is _____ $\times {10}^{ - 9}T$

(Given : Permittivity of vacuum ${ϵ}_{0} = 8.85 \times {10}^{ - 12}{C}^{2}{N}^{ - 1}{m}^{ - 2}$, speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{ - 1}$)
questions.explanation:
The intensity is defined as energy per unit time per unit area. Therefore, $I = \frac{dE}{Adt}$.

Energy density is energy per unit volume. Therefore, ${U}_{d} = \frac{dE}{Adx}$.

Dividing $\frac{I}{{U}_{d}} = \frac{dx}{dt} = c \implies {U}_{d} = \frac{I}{c} = \frac{0.22}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = \frac{22}{3} \times {10}^{ - 10}J{m}^{ - 3}$

Magnetic energy density will be half of total energy density, Therefore, ${U}_{b} = \frac{11}{3} \times {10}^{ - 10}J{m}^{ - 3}$.

Now energy density in magnetic field is given by, ${U}_{b} = \frac{{B}^{2}}{2{\mu }_{0}}$. Therefore,

$\frac{{B}_{\mathrm{rms}}^{2}}{2{\mu }_{0}} = \frac{11}{3} \times {10}^{ - 10}J{m}^{ - 3}$ where ${B}_{\mathrm{rms}}^{2} = \left(\frac{{B}_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \frac{{B}_{0}^{2}}{2} \implies \frac{{B}_{0}^{2}}{4{\mu }_{0}} = \frac{11}{3} \times {10}^{ - 10}\;$

questions.question: The energy density associated with electric field $\vec{E}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ of an electromagnetic wave in free space is given by (${\epsilon }_{0} -$ permittivity of free space, ${\mu }_{0} -$ permeability of free space)
questions.explanation:
When an electromagnetic wave propagates from the source, it transfers energy to the objects in its path. Electric and magnetic fields serve as energy reservoirs for electromagnetic waves. An electromagnetic wave contains the same amount of energy as are contained in the electric and magnetic fields together. In such situation, the energy density of the electromagnetic wave is equal to the sum of the energies of the electric and magnetic fields.

The average electric and magnetic energy densities are given by

$\begin{matrix}{U}_{E} & = & \frac{1}{2}{\epsilon }_{0}{E}^{2} \\ {U}_{B} & = & \frac{1}{2}\frac{{B}^{2}}{{\mu }_{0}}\end{matrix}$

questions.question: The energy associated with electric field is $\left({U}_{E}\right)$ and with magnetic field is $\left({U}_{B}\right)$ for an electromagnetic wave in free space. Then:
questions.explanation:
The average energy density of electric field is given by

Here, ${E}_{0}$ is the maximum value of electric field.

The average energy density of magnetic field is given by

${u}_{B} = \frac{{{B}_{0}}^{2}}{2\mu }$

Here, ${B}_{0}$ is the maximum value of magnetic field.

As the energy density of electric field and magnetic field are equal, the energy associated for equal volume will also be equal.
